In that case, the questions section of Episode #144 - Writers’ Room: Justice Comics, Vol. 1, Issue #527 might interest you. No, seriously.

The also serious answer is that the hodge-podge nature of the new mostly-story-based format means it’s hard to give a general recommendation of what episode to watch. Especially since the questions sections have turned into sort of mini-Editor’s Notes that are sometimes as much about follow up questions from previous episodes as they are about the feature characters of the present episode. :>

I’ve been thinking of how to restructure the Podcast wiki index to reflect it being harder lately to quickly pick out what an episode involves from the title alone, but it’s going to take some brainstorming.

dpt:

Also, bonus points to anyone that finds the major plot hole in this episode. (I posted it in the Spoiler Talk section of the Discord, so don’t look there if you want to play.)

I am guessing it is the fact that C&A messed up how their time dilation was working.

If time runs much faster on the planet, and Progeny crashed there weeks ago and moved on, that means that every minute outside is a much longer period on the planet, not the other way around. From KNYFE’s point of view, she could spend days or weeks on the planet helping to fix things without Progeny being able to get very far away out in space.

I assume they just said it backwards. Obvs it’s more drama if just being on the planet means Knyfe is losing the trail, so hours on the planet = days outside it. or, indeed, we have the old standard of Oops Turns Out Comic Writer Failed Science :P

posts.cooked:
This planet really didn’t need the time dilation element, at least not on the planet; you could say they went through a space distortion on the way here, but once she lands in the planet, she can’t be losing even more time while she deals with these people, Progeny has to have long since come and gone, but she can’t be losing another hour for every second she’s here, or she’d have to just ignore this planet and go chase her quarry without delay.

Adam is right, it’s very comforting to know that one has the right answer about everything.
